source.title: On Uniform Convergence and Low-Norm Interpolation Learning
source.authors: Lijia Zhou; Danica J. Sutherland; N. Srebro

record.tranche_reason: The paper theoretically analyzes interpolation learning and generalization using Gaussian linear regression and uniform-convergence bounds, rather than the empirical neural-network methods in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's results concern low-norm interpolation in a linear-regression setting. Its discussion of deep networks and double descent, and results attributed to other papers, are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves results about Gaussian linear regression and uniform-convergence bounds. None tests the neural-network behaviors specified in V1–V8. Its discussion of interpolation and double descent does not establish a network-width result for V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, two-sided uniform convergence over norm balls or typical algorithm outputs cannot explain consistency in the studied setting. Interpolation-specific bounds can establish consistency and give worst-case asymptotic risk α²σ² for norm factors tending to α≥1. A fixed factor greater than one guarantees bounded risk, while factors tending to one guarantee consistency.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical Gaussian linear regression analysis; no neural-network training recipe or empirical evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: The results depend on Setting B, the junk-feature scale λn, and (for Theorem 4.1) the norm factor αn.

fits_no_version.finding: Minimum-norm interpolation has expected excess population risk tending to zero in Setting B when λn=o(n), taking dJ→∞ before n→∞.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Minimum-norm linear interpolation can be consistent with infinitely many appropriately scaled Gaussian junk features.

fits_no_version.finding: The asymptotic expected worst-case risk among interpolators with norm at most αn times the minimum norm equals α²σ² when αn→α≥1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In Setting B, relative norm inflation quantitatively controls the worst-case asymptotic risk of interpolating linear predictors.

fits_no_version.finding: The expected absolute generalization gap over the minimum-norm ball diverges; typical-output classes for algorithms satisfying Theorem 3.3 have an asymptotic two-sided gap of at least 3σ².
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Two-sided uniform-convergence bounds can fail to explain consistent interpolation in Gaussian linear regression.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 4.3 gives oracle minimum-risk interpolation risk σ²(p−1)/(p−1−n), decreasing with p at fixed n when p>n+1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An oracle minimum-risk linear interpolator benefits from additional dimensions beyond interpolation, but this does not establish the neural-network width claim.

record.problems: The results are theoretical and restricted to the specified Gaussian linear-regression settings; they do not test neural-network architectures or training recipes. No empirical uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy using the same neural architectures and training recipes.
Test error as neural-network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with generalization gaps and comparison with other measures.
Accuracy after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Theoretical results are eligible evidence, but these results address different systems and quantities from V1–V8. The cannot_determine states concern applicability to those versions; they do not dispute the recorded theorem values.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label neural-network comparison.
No network-width sweep or test-error behavior around an interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with other generalization measures.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.

relation.reason: The introduction discusses interpolation learning and double descent as motivation, without testing any specified claim version.

tranche.reason: The theoretical Gaussian linear-regression results concern consistency and uniform-convergence bounds; they neither test nor use the specific neural-network findings in V1–V8.
